instruments.operative_excerpt: 220.3. (a) An employee or a contractor of a school district, county office of education, charter school, or state special school for the blind or the deaf shall not be required to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent unless otherwise required by state or federal law. (b) Subdivision (a) does not constitute a change in, but is declaratory of, existing law. || 220.5. (a) A school district, county office of education, charter school, state special school for the blind or the deaf, or a member of the governing board of a school district or county office of education or a member of the governing body of a charter school, shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law. (b) Subdivision (a) does not constitute a change in, but is declaratory of, existing law. (c) Any policy, regulation, guidance, directive, or other action of a school district, county office of education, charter school, or state special school for the blind or the deaf, or a member of the governing board of a school district or county office of education or a member of the governing body of a charter school, that is inconsistent with subdivision (a) is invalid and shall not have any force or effect.
other_subjects: Sec. 3 / Ed Code 217: State Department of Education to develop resources and supports for parents, guardians and families of LGBTQ pupils (grades 7-12)
Sec. 4 / Ed Code 220.1: anti-retaliation protection for employees who support a pupil in exercising rights, or who teach consistent with state standards and the California Healthy Youth Act
Sec. 2: legislative findings (e.g. "Policies that forcibly \"out\" pupils without their consent remove opportunities for LGBTQ+ young people and their families to build trust")
Digest classifies as one subject: "pupil rights"; the bill bundles disclosure ban + family-support resources + employee anti-retaliation
coauthors: Principal coauthors Assembly: Cervantes, Jackson, Lee, Low, Zbur
Principal coauthors Senate: Atkins, Eggman, Laird, Menjivar, Padilla, Wiener

instruments.history_note: Assembly ayes/noes per history: 75-0 (4/25/24), Senate 29-8 (6/13/24), concurrence 61-16 (6/27/24). Approved by Governor 2024-07-15, Chapter 95, Statutes of 2024.

instruments.operative_excerpt: (17) (A) Notwithstanding any other law, including Section 6924 of the Family Code and Section 124260 of the Health and Safety Code, to be notified in writing within three days from the date any teacher, counselor, or employee of the school becomes aware that their child is doing either of the following: (i) Identifying at school as a gender that does not align with the child’s sex on their birth certificate, other official records, or sex assigned at birth. (ii) Using sex-segregated school programs and activities, including athletic teams and competitions, or using facilities that do not align with the child’s sex on their birth certificate, other official records, or sex assigned at birth.
other_subjects: Amends Ed Code 51101 (parental rights list); also notice about sex-segregated programs, athletic teams and facilities (same notification right); legislative-intent subparagraph (B)
instruments.history_note: Referred to Assembly Education (and Judiciary); amended 2023-03-09 and 2023-08-23; re-referred to Ed 2023-08-24; "Died pursuant to Art. IV, Sec. 10(c) of the Constitution" 2024-01-31. No committee or floor vote recorded.

instruments.operative_excerpt: (10) To have access to the official and unofficial school records of their child.
other_subjects: Amends Ed Code 51101 only; does not mention gender identity, name or pronouns. Peripheral: expands parental access to unofficial school records.
instruments.history_note: Assembly Education 2025-04-09: "Failed passage" (committee vote 2 Ayes, 5 Noes per BILL_SUMMARY_VOTE_TBL); no floor vote.

instruments.operative_excerpt: "Pupil instruction: transgender concepts: opt out" - parents may excuse child from curriculum referencing transgender concepts (not a notification-of-identity bill).
other_subjects: Curriculum opt-out; private right of action
instruments.history_note: Died at Desk 2026-02-02. No vote. Instruction opt-out, not parental notification of a pupil name/gender change; listed as peripheral.

instruments.operative_excerpt: SB 622 (Grove): "(2) A pupil’s participation in sex-segregated school programs and activities, including athletic teams and competitions, shall be consistent with the pupil’s sex at birth." AB 844 (Essayli) similar plus facilities.
other_subjects: Sports/facilities by sex; no parental-notification clause
instruments.history_note: Peripheral; sports and facilities, not parental notification. Not vote-checked.

own_words.excerpt: By order of Newsom & School Administrators teachers were told NOT to share information with parents, that's crazy. Newsom & Administrators STOLE the authority to hide information from parents - restore parental rights.
own_words.note: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey completed 2026, 'Campaign themes' answer. Names no bill; opposes policy of not telling parents (points toward options 3-5 side vs 1-2; not coded).

own_words.excerpt: No Indoctrination The indoctrination policies like AB957 in California leads teenagers to transgender without proper maturity, resulting in lifelong regrets. AB957 focuses on amending the judicial criteria used to determine custodial rights in family court proceedings. Specifically, it proposes to include parental affirmation of their child's chosen gender as an additional factor considered in custody decisions. This provision would be misused and lead to allegations of child abuse if parents do not affirm their child's gender identity. AB957 clearly took away parent’s right to guide their children to make the proper choice. We must say NO to AB957 !
own_words.note: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey completed in 2024 (page says 2026 survey not yet completed). Names AB 957 (family law: gender identity, custody) which is NOT a school parental-notification bill; direction-only for this question.

initiative.note: Students First: Protect Kids California initiatives (school parental notification of gender identity among three measures) FAILED to qualify for the 2024 ballot; organizers said they would target 2026. No evidence found that any such measure is on the Nov 2026 ballot (not verified against Secretary of State list).
initiative.excerpt: The organization Students First: Protect Kids California started too late to consolidate their three separate initiatives into one, and its signature-gathering came up short of the 546,651 verifiable signatures that had to be collected within six months to make the presidential election ballot.
